title: Callahan
name: Callahan
metaTitle: Callahan 1031 Exchange Services in Jacksonville, FL
metaDescription: Callahan 1031 exchange coordination for rail-adjacent land and small-format distribution replacement property north of Jacksonville.

sections.html:
Callahan sits in Nassau County north of Jacksonville along US 1 and near the I-95 corridor, and its replacement-property scope is thin by design: rural and agricultural land background, a small-town commercial core, and a growing but still limited amount of distribution space spilling north from Jacksonville's industrial growth. A specification package for this market has to acknowledge that scale honestly rather than overstate it.

A submittal package for Callahan should lead with actual utility and access documentation rather than a growth narrative, since the market's value proposition rests on specific site fundamentals rather than broad population trends.

sections.heading: Rural and Distribution Scope North of Jacksonville
sections.html:
Most of the land around Callahan remains agricultural or rural-residential, and the commercial and industrial inventory that does exist has grown up along US 1 and near the I-95 interchange as Jacksonville's northside industrial base has expanded outward. CSX rail lines run through Nassau County near the town, giving a small number of parcels rail-adjacent characteristics that do not extend to the broader area.

Nassau County's population growth has trailed the coastal Yulee and Amelia Island areas considerably, and Callahan's commercial development has followed that slower pace, which keeps the market genuinely small rather than an undervalued growth story waiting to be discovered.

sections.heading: Property Types
sections.html:
Callahan's identification lists draw from a narrow, honestly small set of categories:

  • small-format distribution buildings near US 1 and I-95
  • rail-adjacent land suited to future industrial development
  • small-town retail and service buildings along US 1
  • agricultural land with industrial rezoning potential
  • self-storage parcels serving the surrounding rural population

Of these, only the small-format distribution category and select rail-adjacent parcels typically trade at price points consistent with a mid-size exchange, and the remaining categories should be sized to a smaller replacement basis.

sections.heading: US 1/I-95 Corridor Specifications
sections.html:
Access specifications should be verified against actual road classification rather than assumed from the town's name, since properties fronting US 1 have different truck-access characteristics than those set back on rural county roads. Any distribution building in this corridor should be reviewed for its actual drive time to I-95 rather than straight-line distance, since Nassau County's road network does not always provide a direct route.

Well and septic service is still common on parcels away from the immediate US 1 frontage, and a buyer underwriting an industrial conversion should confirm municipal water and sewer availability before assuming it as a baseline utility.

sections.heading: Land and Rail-Adjacent Diligence Items
sections.html:
Rail-adjacent land near Callahan should be reviewed for actual spur rights and CSX easement documentation before it is treated as rail-served in an underwriting model, since proximity to a rail line does not by itself confer service rights. Agricultural land being considered for a future industrial exchange should be checked against current Nassau County zoning and any required rezoning timeline before it is added to an identification list, since rezoning approval can take longer than a standard 180-day exchange period allows.

A survey confirming actual parcel boundaries and any wetlands delineation should be obtained early, since rural Nassau County parcels are more likely than urban Duval County land to carry unresolved boundary or wetlands questions that a title report alone will not surface.

sections.heading: Sequencing for Small-Town Inventory
sections.html:
Given how few qualifying properties turn over in Callahan at any one time, exchangers should carry a Yulee or broader Nassau County I-95 corridor identification alongside a Callahan property as a practical backup, since both draw on the same north-of-Jacksonville industrial spillover logic. Qualified intermediary coordination should begin early, and buyers should be candid with lenders about the market's small transaction scale rather than model it against Jacksonville metro comparables.

A pre-cleared lender familiar with rural Nassau County collateral shortens the path from identification to closing meaningfully, given how few local comparables exist for an appraiser to draw on in this market.

faqs.q: How much industrial inventory actually exists in Callahan?
faqs.a: A limited amount. The area remains largely agricultural and rural-residential, with distribution and industrial development concentrated near US 1 and the I-95 interchange as Jacksonville's northside industrial base spills outward, and a buyer should expect a short list of qualifying properties rather than a deep pipeline.

faqs.q: Does proximity to a CSX rail line mean a parcel is rail-served?
faqs.a: Not automatically. Actual spur rights and easement documentation should be confirmed with CSX before a parcel is treated as rail-served in an underwriting model, and a buyer should request that documentation directly rather than rely on a listing description.

faqs.q: Can agricultural land near Callahan be identified for an industrial exchange?
faqs.a: Yes, but any required rezoning should be checked against current Nassau County timelines first, since approval can take longer than a standard 180-day exchange period allows, and a buyer should have a fallback plan in case rezoning is not completed before the exchange must close.

faqs.q: What backup submarket pairs with Callahan?
faqs.a: Yulee and the broader Nassau County I-95 corridor draw on the same north-of-Jacksonville industrial spillover logic and function as a practical backup identification.

faqs.q: Should Callahan transaction sizes be modeled against Jacksonville metro comparables?
faqs.a: No. The market's scale is genuinely smaller, and lenders should be given an honest picture of local transaction sizes rather than comparables drawn from Southside or Westside, since overstating the market's depth can lead to a financing package that does not match what actually trades in Callahan.
